input.content: Pattern: "simplifying" a cleanup/teardown function by dropping an ownership/identity guard before an unconditional delete. Symptom: a cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id) replaced `if active[workspace_id].setup_id == setup_id: pop` with an unconditional `active.pop(workspace_id)`. The guard was load-bearing: when a stale/failed entity's queued cleanup runs AFTER a newer entity has already taken the same slot, the unconditional delete wipes the newer entity's live record (cross-entity data loss). Review rule: when a diff removes a check-then-delete guard keyed on an identity/version field, treat the guard as load-bearing until proven otherwise — reconstruct the interleaving where the deleted record is owned by a DIFFERENT id than the one being cleaned up. Existing tests that only exercise the same-id path pass and hide the regression. Confirm against the documented contract ("removes any association IT OWNS"). Severity P1: scoped, recoverable data loss, violates documented invariant.
